title: WIC participation in August 2026
question: What will USDA FNS report in the first official publication of August 2026 national WIC Total Participants, including women, infants, and children, without seasonal adjustment, expressed in millions?
resolutionSource: USDA FNS WIC Data Tables, Monthly Data - National Level
resolutionRule: Resolve on the first official publication of August 2026 national Total Participants in the WIC monthly participation table identified by the registered source binding. Convert person counts to millions by dividing by 1,000,000; if the source reports thousands, multiply by 0.001. Preserve the precision of the published count. Freeze the first published value and disregard subsequent revisions or corrections, including same-day corrections. The registered target and source-host restriction remain unchanged; discrepancies in the conversion factor and current official hosting are documented in reasoning.

reasoning.text: August 2026 WIC national participation first-print forecast

The target is the national monthly Total Participants count for women, infants, and children, as published without seasonal adjustment. The matching series also appears in Keydata Table 21: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program (WIC). HistoricalContext contains current published monthly observations from the September 11, 2026 data vintage, not certified original first prints. Archived initial-month Keydata vintages are separately identified as early-vintage proxies.

reasoning.call: Fetch https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/sites/default/files/resource-files/37wic-monthly-9.pdf through the official WIC Data Tables page.
reasoning.result: National Total Participants: October 2025 6,909,938; November 6,771,734; December 6,712,611; January 2026 6,696,300; February 6,664,741; March 6,703,035; April 6,708,518; May 6,687,977; June 6,669,554. FY2026 figures are preliminary and subject to revision.

reasoning.call: Read historical June and August national Total Participants from the same official monthly PDF.

reasoning.text: The outside-view base rate is persistence from June, with a seasonal adjustment estimated from the three fetched June-to-August comparisons. Their changes are -10,254, +93,402, and +27,908 participants, averaging +37,018.667 participants. This gives a seasonal persistence prior of 6.706572667 million.

reasoning.call: Fetch archived January, February, and April 2026 Keydata PDFs listed in sourceContext and read each report's latest-month participation value in Table 21.
reasoning.result: January's archived count was 6,689,525 versus the current 6,696,300; February's was 6,640,819 versus 6,664,741; April's was 6,704,900 versus 6,708,518. Subsequent upward revisions were 6,775, 23,922, and 3,618 participants. These archives are initial-month vintage proxies; their chronology against the first publication of the separate national monthly table was not certified.

reasoning.call: Fetch https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/wic/fr-042926 for the income eligibility mechanism applying during the target month.
reasoning.result: Guidelines effective July 1, 2026 retain the maximum income criterion of 185% of poverty. For a four-person household in the contiguous-state schedule, the maximum is $61,050 annually or $5,088 monthly.

reasoning.text: Level: June anchors the forecast at 6.669554 million. Momentum: April-to-June participation fell by 38,964 people; extrapolating half that two-month decline subtracts 0.019482 million. Reporting mechanism: the three archived-to-current revisions average 0.011438333 million, which is subtracted as a small early-vintage proxy adjustment. Policy: the annual July eligibility update could support enrollment, but no fetched enrollment response identifies a separate numerical effect; routine summer effects remain in the seasonal adjustment. No additional one-off adjustment is quantified.

Prior/update/interval: Use seasonal persistence with damped recent momentum and an early-vintage proxy correction. The historical sample is nine monthly levels from October 2025 through June 2026, plus three June-to-August seasonal comparisons and three archived revision pairs. Point = 6.669554 + 0.037018667 - 0.019482 - 0.011438333 = 6.675652333 million. Across the eight successive monthly changes, sigma = 0.051951446 million. The normal-approximation one-month half-width is 1.28*sigma = 0.066497850 million; multiplying by sqrt(2) for the two-month horizon gives 0.094042162 million. Final rounded bounds are 6.581610 and 6.769694 million. This is a model-based 80% interval; the small archive sample does not establish complete first-print error calibration.

Ledger discrepancies: the fetched monthly table reports persons, so the registered multiplication factor 0.001 would be incorrect unless its input were first converted to thousands. This forecast preserves the registered unit and converts persons directly to millions. USDA's official April 30, 2026 announcement identifies the Food and Nutrition Administration as formerly FNS; current pages and documents were accessed through its official hosting mirror. The registered allowlist contains only www.fns.usda.gov, so current hosting may require resolver metadata review. The target identifier and registered resolution URL remain unchanged.

Release-date verification failed: the official program pages expose historical publication dates but no fetched official calendar or announcement established the August 2026 table's future release date. Searches and attempted calendar endpoints did not verify a date. resolutionDate is therefore null rather than inferred from cadence or the supplied window. This leaves the required calendar validation unmet.

Upside risk: stronger summer enrollment, faster certification, or a reporting backlog clearance could lift participation above 6.769694 million. Downside risk: continued enrollment losses, slower recertification, or missing state submissions could push it below 6.581610 million. A large administrative reporting disruption or an unusually strong response to eligibility implementation could land outside the interval.
